title: Woondum National Park

beo.heading: Woondum National Park
paras: Woondum National Park covers about 4,000 hectares of steep ranges between Cooran, Kin Kin and Mothar Mountain. It was long managed as State forest, and in 2009 it became a national park. The Queensland Government records the name as reportedly coming from Kabi words for blue tongue lizard and place. Tall eucalypt forest covers the ridges, with rainforest in the sheltered gullies and creeks tumbling over boulders below. Foresters prized Woondum's spotted gums because they resist a fungal leaf and shoot disease, and seed from here went to plantations across south east Queensland. The park holds fourteen regional ecosystems, including endangered gallery rainforest, and records of koalas, sooty owls, plumed frogmouths and the tusked frog. The Kabi Kabi First Nation holds deep connections here, and the Mothar Mountain rock pools and Kabi Boys Creek are significant cultural sites.
